To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the genotype of HCV RNA-dependent RNA-polymerases (RdRps) has an impact on their enzymatic activity and oligomerisation.
the de novo activity and polymerase cooperativity differ significantly between HCV genotypes 1 and the remaining genotypes.

the de novo activity and the oligomerization of NS5B polymerases of different genotypes are different and that these differences are probably related to structural differences in the αF and αF helixes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genotype-specific differences in NS5Bs de novo activity and NS5B-5B interactions, which could be useful for the design of genotype-specific antivirals targeting the NS5B.
the characterization of NS5B de-novo activity and oligomerisation of different genotypes and the identification of regions involved in NS5A-NS5B and NS5B- NS5B interaction.
the characterization of NS5B polymerases from different HCV genotypes and subgenotypes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
genotype 1 has a lower de novo activity than the other genotypes, which is mainly due to differences at the structural level and not to differences in the catalytic residues.
the genotype of HCV influences NS5B polymerization and de novo activity, and that the αF helical region is probably involved in this process.
genotype 1 polymerase has the lowest Vmax, the highest Hill coefficient and oligomeric structure, and the lowest de novo activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the de novo polymerase activity of NS5Bs from genotypes 3 and 5 was lower than that of genotype 1, and the NS5Bs from these genotypes showed lower cooperativity and oligomerization than genotype 1.
the NS5B genotype diversity has a direct impact on the de novo activity and NS5B- NS5B interaction.
genotype-specific differences in NS5Bs are reflected in differences in de novo activity, oligomerization, and interaction of the αT and αF helixes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NS5B polymerases from different genotypes are not identical, and this should be taken into account when designing antivirals against HCV.
genotype 1 polymerases have lower de novo activity and higher oligomerization than the other studied genotypes.
the NS5B de-novo activity is not only genotype dependent but also that it can be modulated by the presence of the αF helices.
